Overview

Account first, then the thing they came to start

Your direction from the §326 walk: every way to start something asks for the account alone, and the team, league or organization is named after the email is confirmed. This page shows the four sign-ups today and after, the Home page someone lands on if they wander off, and sign-in for an account that is still waiting.

Stays as it is

  • Registering a team for a tournament. The registration still goes to the organizer before the coach verifies (V2), so organizers never wait on a coach's inbox.
  • Invitations, family claims, joining a team, following a team. These already ask for the account alone.
  • Someone already signed in still goes straight to step 2 from any of the four.
  • One tap to create (V1). Step 2 still makes the team on a tap, never automatically, so a link opened twice cannot make two teams.

A5The Founding Season offer for an organization created after the link

Ruled 2026-10-18Count from the day the account was made

Today the offer attaches at the sign-up click, because the organization is created then. After, the organization is created after the link. The sign-up window closes at the end of December 31, 2026. Counting from the account means someone who signs up on the 31st and confirms on January 2 still gets it. The offer ends September 30, 2027 for everyone, so creating the organization later gains nothing extra.

Not chosen: Count from the day the organization is created

Pricing sends the plan and billing choice to the sign-up, and production drops both. The account will remember them, so the plan step opens with that plan chosen. The person can still change it.

Product-manager brief

Account-First Sign-up — PM brief

Status: drawn and design-reviewed 2026-10-18; all seven asks ruled as recommended the same day. Part 1 (Start a team, Start a league, Home's finish card, sign-in's Send the link again) built and committed 8647a4e8 2026-10-18; owner walk §336 owed. Home's finish card revised 2026-10-19 (a workspace that waits for its name; drawn, OK'd by the owner and built the same day; §336's W3 and W5 rewritten, W16–W17 added). Parts 2 (Run a tournament) and 3 (Coach Premium) next. Plan: ACCOUNT_FIRST_SIGNUP_PLAN.md.

What changes for the person signing up

Every way to start something on FieldLogicHQ — run a tournament, start a team, start a league, Coach Premium — asks for the same four things first: first name, last name, email, password. The person confirms their email. The link brings them to the one thing they came to make: name the team, the league or the organization (and, for Coach Premium, pick the sport and billing before checkout). Nothing is asked twice, and the page says from the start that naming comes next.

If they open the email on another device, or come back days later and sign in, FieldLogicHQ still knows what they came to start and takes them there. Home keeps a place for it under Workspaces — "Your team, not named yet" — until they name it, and then that same card carries the team's name. Nothing to dismiss, and nothing to lose (revised 2026-10-19; it was a "Finish creating your team" card with Not now).

Why it matters

  • Nothing is built for an unproven email. Today the tournament sign-up creates the organization, takes its web address and starts its Founding Season offer before anyone opens the link. Abandoned sign-ups leave live organizations behind, and an address typed by someone else can claim a club's name.
  • Nothing typed is lost. Today the paid team sign-up forgets the team, sport and billing choice when the link opens in another tab or device, and the plan picked on the pricing page never reaches the plan step.
  • One sign-up to learn, test and support instead of four different forms.

Customer impact

Every new coach and organizer meets this on day one. The number of steps stays the same: one form, one email, one name. The trade: the check-your-email screen can no longer name the team, because it has not been named yet.

Tournament registration, invitations and family claims do not change.

Priority

High. It removes the organization-before-proof gap on the revenue sign-up and the "asked twice" confusion the owner hit on the first walk of the verified sign-up. It sits on screens that went live on 2026-10-18, so it should land before those screens see real traffic.

Success criteria

  • No organization, team or league exists for an email that has not been confirmed.
  • A sign-up opened on a second device lands on the right create step with the pricing choice intact.
  • No one who confirmed their email lands on a page with no way to start what they came for.
  • The owner's walk of each of the four doors reads as one account step and one naming step.

Why

Owner, 2026-10-18, walking §326: "why do we ask them to create a team name twice?" The free team sign-up asks for the team name on its first form, then brings the coach back from the email link to a second form with the name filled in and one tap to create (V1, ruled 2026-10-16 for its reason: an automatic create would make a second team from a link opened twice). Filled in or not, the second screen reads as being asked again.

Owner direction, same day: "users create accounts first (no org, tournament, team name, etc) then after confirmation do the create steps based on where they came from." The census below makes the case stronger than tidiness.

What the code does today (census 2026-10-18)

Nine doors make an account while signed out. Four start something new; five make the account on the way to something else.

DoorAsks before the linkMade before the linkComes back to
Run a tournament (/auth/signup)organization, first, last, email, passwordthe organization, its address, the owner seat and the Founding Season compthe organization's plan step
Start a team (/start/team)team name, first, last, email, passwordthe account onlythe same page, name filled in, one tap
Start a league (/start/league, beta)league name, first, last, email, passwordthe account onlythe same page, name filled in, one tap
Coach Premium (/coaches/start, /coaches/claim/[token])team, sport, billing, first, last, email, passwordthe account onlythe same page; the details survive only in that browser tab
Account only (/auth/signup?account=1), family claim, join, follow nudgefirst, last, email, passwordthe account onlywhere they were going
Tournament registration (/{org}/{t}/register)the registration, then the accountthe registration (V2, on purpose)the join page, which links it

Findings (each has a flag on the hub's drawings):

  • F01 — The tournament sign-up builds the organization before the email is proven. app/api/auth/signup/route.ts makes the auth user (L268–300), then the organization with its slug (L303), the owner membership (L312) and the Founding Season comp_period override (L326–338), all before the link is opened. An abandoned sign-up leaves a live organization; an address typed by someone who does not own it still takes the club's name and URL.
  • F02 — The paid team sign-up forgets what was typed. Team, sport and billing live only in a sessionStorage draft (app/team/TeamSignupClient.tsx L181–217). A link opened in another tab or on another device comes back blank. Its route (app/api/auth/team-signup/route.ts) has no sign-up throttle (the coach sign-up has one, 7bbfbebb) and its check-your-email state has no Send the link again.
  • F03 — The plan picked on the pricing page is dropped in production. Pricing links to /auth/signup?plan=&billing=; the page reads them only on the instant (verification off) path, and the verification redirect is hard-coded to ?choosePlan=1 (route.ts L275). Onboarding reads only billing; featuredPlan is fixed to Tournament Plus.
  • F04 — The team and league name is asked before the link and shown again after it. It travels in the link (?team= / ?league= with confirmed=1) and returns in an editable field under the same heading, which reads as a second ask.
  • F05 — A confirmed account with nothing started has no way to start. Home shows "Nothing here yet — follow a team, tournament, or organization" (components/consumer/HomePersonalization.tsx L231) and no start door; the persona Start menu lives in the top bar. Account-first makes this state common: everyone who confirms and walks away lands here.
  • F06 — A waiting account that signs in is told to verify, with no way to get the link again (found by /docs 2026-10-17, recorded on the Verify Every Sign-up memory).

Scope

In: the four "start something" doors — Run a tournament, Start a team, Start a league, Coach Premium (including the claim link) — plus the shared check-your-email state, the Home landing for an account with nothing started, and Send the link again on sign-in for a waiting account.

Out, deliberately:

  • Tournament registration keeps V2: the registration goes to the organizer before the coach verifies, so organizers are never blind to a coach who never opens the email.
  • Invites (the assistant invite's instant path, org member invites), family claims, the join page and the follow nudge already ask for the account alone.
  • R1 (pre-hijack by password, accepted 2026-10-17) is unchanged by this work.

The end state

  1. One account step for every start door. First name, last name, email, password. Headed with the door's own name (Create Your Team Home, Run Your Tournament, Start Your Season, Coach Premium) and a line that says what comes next (A1, A2).
  2. One check-your-email state, the Verify Every Sign-up block: the address, Send the link again, Use a different email (keeps the entries), Already verified? Sign in. It names what is next ("…then you'll name your team"), not a name the person has not typed yet.
  3. The link lands on the door's create step (A3) — the signed-in screens that already exist: Adding a team (team name), Adding a league (league name), the add-organization form (organization name, then the plan step), the Premium form (team, sport, billing, then checkout). The field is empty and focused; the screen says "Step 2 of 2".
  4. The account remembers where it came from, not the browser and not only the link: the door, and the pricing page's plan and billing when there were any, are written onto the account at sign-up (auth user_metadata.start). The link, the sign-in destination and Home all read it, so a laptop sign-up opened on a phone still lands on the right step (F02, F03).
  5. Home finishes what was started (A4). An account with an unfinished start sees "Finish setting up your team" at the top of Home until it creates one or dismisses the card; an account with nothing sees a way to start something on a phone as well as a computer.
  6. Sign-in offers Send the link again to a waiting account (A7, F06).
  7. The tournament door makes the organization after the link (F01). The Founding Season comp attaches when the organization is made; whether the window is counted from the account or the organization is A5. The plan picked on the pricing page is chosen on the plan step (A6).

Rulings (owner, 2026-10-18 — all seven as recommended)

  • A1 One account form for every start door, in the warm start look (startForm.module.css), headed with each door's own name. Coach Premium keeps its sales page; only its setup card changes.
  • A2 A two-step line on both steps ("1 Your account · 2 Your team / league / organization"), reusing the tournament registration page's step-bar shape (register.module.css .steps) in warm tokens; not clickable.
  • A3 The link lands straight on the create step, field empty and focused. V1 holds: one tap creates, never automatic.
  • A4 Home shows a finish card ("Finish creating your team" / league / organization; Coach Premium: "Finish setting up your Coaches Portal" + Continue setup) only to an account that came from a start door and has not finished. Not now hides it until the next sign-in; a second Not now hides it for good. "Nothing here yet" is hidden while it shows. Revised 2026-10-19 — see A4 revised below.
  • A5 The Founding Season offer counts from the day the account was made: an account created before the sign-up close (FOUNDING_SEASON_SIGNUP_CLOSE, end of 2026-12-31) still gets the comp when its organization is created after it. The comp's end date is fixed for everyone (FOUNDING_SEASON_END), so a late organization gains nothing. Logged in BUSINESS_DECISIONS.md 2026-10-18 (refines 2026-09-07 part 2). Edges Decided 2026-10-19 (owner, Part 2 build session, each as recommended): (a) after the close only the creation the account's start sign-up came for counts — read from a locked copy of the door on app_metadata, since the remembered door is the account holder's to edit; (b) the same rule for Coach Premium (Part 3); (c) the plan step honours it — after the close, an organization that got the comp when it was made picks Tournament Plus at $0 on its first plan choice only. Eligibility reads the auth user's created_at and the locked door, never user_metadata.
  • A6 The pricing page's plan and billing ride on the account and open the plan step with that plan chosen; the person can still change it.
  • A7 Sign-in offers Send the link again to a waiting account, in this project, with the resend's existing limit.

Design review 2026-10-18 (D1–D12, on the hub's Decisions tab) is part of the drawings these rulings approved: no icon well on phone start forms, the plain "Your email is confirmed." sentence, 44px foot links, "Create Account" in the start forms and "Create account" on the Premium card, the resend inside the sign-in error box.

A4 revised (owner, 2026-10-19)

Why: walking §336, two taps on Not now left the account on "Nothing here yet — follow a team" with no way back to the team it came to start (F05 was fixed only while the card showed; the plan's promise above, "an account with nothing sees a way to start something", was never built). Owner direction: a pending workspace that stays on Home for good, with no team name, so it is always there without being a nagging message, and it fills in with the team once it is named.

Ruled the same day:

  • It shows beside every other workspace, not only when there is none: *"otherwise they lose that team … it should look like a second team they still owe if it truly is."*
  • Wording: Coaches Portal · Not named yet · Name your team; no plan badge (nothing to price yet); Coach Premium has its own words, Setup not finished · Continue setup.
  • A way for a fan (an account that never came from a start door) to start something stays out of this project.

Held from standing rulings: it is a placeholder drawn from the remembered door, never a real nameless team, league or organization — a real row would bring back F01's orphans and V1's second-team-from-a-link-opened-twice, and would flip every rule that asks whether the account has a workspace. Nothing is made until the name is typed and Create is tapped.

As drawn (hub Home screen, v7; OK'd 2026-10-19): the real Home workspace card, unchanged in frame; three slots differ — an amber Not named yet badge (the warm badge ink), the title Your team, and Name your team in the meta line's place, olive, in the sans at 12px because it is the one thing on the card that must be read (/design D13). The whole card opens step 2; its one door mark is the chevron every workspace card carries (D14). Solid edge — dashed already means a record that left a list (D16). /design 2026-10-19 D13–D17 are on the hub's Decisions tab. It sits after the workspaces already in use. League and organization wait as the Admin Area card they become (blue icon well); Coach Premium as a Coaches Portal card. Two free teams already share one Home card ("Your teams · N teams"), so for a coach who also assists on another free team, the waiting card folds into that one when named rather than filling in alone (today's rule, unchanged).

OK'd by the owner 2026-10-19 ("I approve") and built the same day. What the build changed:

  • Home: the finish card becomes the waiting workspace, inside the Workspaces section; "Nothing here yet" stays hidden while it shows (Home is not empty).
  • The card's rule drops the no-workspace condition (owner: every case) and the Not now count. The Not now write, its route and the session sign-in-time read (sessionSignedInAt, getClaims() amr) go with it; notNow/notNowAt on existing accounts are simply ignored.
  • It goes when the thing is made by any route. **The finish card hid itself once there was any workspace, so only two paths cleared the door; now that the card shows beside every workspace, a missed path is a "Not named yet" card next to the real team.** Census 2026-10-19 (helper, cited lines read): clearStartDoor is now also called by provisionStandaloneTeamWorkspace once committed (every Coach Premium team: the checkout's comp and mock paths, both Stripe webhook events) and by linkTournamentRegistrationToBasicCoachTeam when it creates or adopts a free team (the join page; a signed-in tournament registration). Deliberately not cleared: a staff seat (owner: "otherwise they lose that team"), a season rollover, a team moved into a club, and a tournament organization from the add-organization form — not the team or league the door came to start; the organization door and its clear are Part 2's.
  • The waiting card is the Home workspace card itself (WaitingWorkspaceCard, WAITING_WORKSPACE in lib/start-door.ts): the family's label, icon and accent; the amber badge Home already uses; the step as .wsAction (sans, 0.75rem, olive). The payload field is waitingWorkspace: { door } (no email: the card no longer says "You confirmed …"). Gone: startCardVisible, withNotNow, sessionSignedInAt, recordStartDoorNotNow, POST /api/account/start-door, the .start* styles.
  • The league card keeps today's rule: only while Start a league can open (the beta is on and no invitation waits).
  • Walk §336: W3 and W5 rewritten (saved under their own keys, so old ticks never land on new steps); W4 and W6 reworded; W16 (Coach Premium takes the waiting card's place, localhost) and W17 (beside a team they help with, staging after the push) added. Help: the two answers that named the finish card (coaches first login; platform-admin Confirm Email) say what Home shows now.
  • Guard tests/unit/account-first-signup.test.ts pins the new rule, the card, and every clear above.

Fixed in /review (high risk, four lenses, 2026-10-19):

  • A waiting league that could never open (High): /start/league and /api/league/create turn away an account already in a real organization, and the finish card's no-workspace rule had been hiding that case. The league door's card now carries all three of the page's gates (beta on, no pending invite, !userBelongsToOtherRealOrg).
  • Only a matching door clears (Medium, two lenses): clearStartDoor(userId, fulfils) — a free team or a claim clears team; a Premium team clears team and premium; a league clears league. **This supersedes Part 1's build call "creating either a team or a league clears the door"**, made while the card hid itself on any workspace (so the cross-clear was invisible); under "beside every workspace", a team made by a league-door account would have wiped the league it still owes.
  • The card's link has no aria-label of its own: like every workspace card, its name is what it shows, so the visible "Coaches Portal" / "Admin Area" is in it (label in name). The "route is gone" test resolves from the repo root.
  • Help search keywords gain "not named yet" (the old "finish creating your team" stays, for people who remember it).

Accepted, left as they are: a failed clear (an auth hiccup, logged) leaves the card beside the real team until a later creation of that kind — Stripe's retry takes the already-provisioned path, which does not clear; a door set by hand in the account's own metadata can show a card for organization/premium whose page then turns the person away (their own Home only; nothing gated is exposed); accounts made on staging since 8647a4e8 that made a team by Premium or a claim keep their door until they make another (no backfill: staging-only, about a day). Part 2 must call clearStartDoor(user.id, ['organization']) wherever an organization is made for the account (/api/org/create and the new step 2), or the organization door's card stays beside the real organization.

Build order (one build, three parts, each shippable alone)

  1. Shared pieces + team + league. The account step, the remembered door, the link landing, Home's card and start door, sign-in's resend. Team and league are already half there, so they prove the shared pieces on the lowest-risk doors.
  2. Run a tournament + the pricing plan. The organization moves after the link; the Founding comp moves with it; the plan rides on the account. Before this part ships, count (read-only, owner-approved) the organizations on production made by sign-ups that never confirmed; cleaning them is a separate owner call (the platform admin's empty-organization filter already finds them).
  3. Coach Premium + the claim link. Account first, then team, sport and billing, then checkout. The route gets the coach sign-up's throttle and the resend.

Notes for the build

  • Links already in people's inboxes (?team=/?league= with confirmed=1) keep filling in for one release.
  • Signed-in people at any door keep going straight to the create step, as today.
  • The org sign-up's public-address field: today the address is checked before the account; it moves to the create step with the name. Confirm from the add-organization form whether it offers the address field before building.

Fixed in /review (high risk, five lenses):

  • last_sign_in_at is re-stamped by the auth service on every token refresh, so "Not now until the next sign-in" would have meant about an hour. The card reads the session's own sign-in time (the access token's amr, via getClaims(), only for a once-dismissed card).

The Founding Season rule (A5 + edges ratified 2026-10-19). One rule, isFoundingSeasonOpenFor(accountCreatedAt, cameToStart) in lib/plan-config.ts, read through foundingSeasonOfferFor(user, creates) in lib/founding-season.ts by /api/org/create and /api/league/create (Part 3 adds create-team-checkout). The locked door is app_metadata.start_door, written by lockStartDoorOrUndo at sign-up for the doors that carry an offer (organization, league, premium) — a failed lock undoes the account — and cleared by clearStartDoor with the remembered door. The plan step after the close: foundingSeasonOfferOnPlanChoice(org) (a live Founding comp row while the plan is still the first-run choice — no tournament, no saved setup work, onboarding not finished, lib/first-run-plan.ts, the same lock the free-plan route applies; server facts only; fails closed) gates create-checkout's no-Stripe Tournament Plus and, through founding-season-status?planChoice=1, the plan card's $0 (PricingSection foundingOfferHeld, Tournament Plus only). The onboarding plan route is not a grant path (census 2026-10-19: it only schedules the upsell email), so it was left on the window. The Club exclusion holds: every creation makes a tournament org, and the plan-step rule checks foundingCompAppliesToPlan.

Production count (owner-approved read, 2026-10-19): 5 organizations; 1 made by a sign-up that never confirmed (made 2026-08-29, free Tournament plan, no tournaments, owner never signed in, holds a Founding comp). Cleaning it is a separate owner call. Probe: .probe/account-first/prod-unconfirmed-orgs.mjs (read-only; slugs to a local file only).

How "first plan choice" (ruling (c)) is read — flagged to the owner 2026-10-19, not a ruling. The plan step's own "plan chosen" mark is written by the browser and wiped by every first-run plan change (the free-plan route, an abandoned checkout), so /review showed an owner could reopen $0 by starting a checkout and walking away. The build reads the first plan choice as the first-run choice: while the plan is still editable on the plan step (before setup starts) Tournament Plus stays $0 for an organization holding the comp, even if it picked free a minute earlier; once a tournament or setup work exists, an upgrade pays the list price. A strictly-first-click reading needs a server-side record of the first choice (a schema change) — the owner's call.

/simplify (2026-10-19, four lenses): one lockStartDoorOrUndo for both sign-up routes; the org sign-up answers an existing account one way (409, as account-only always did) and has one response shape; ensureFoundingSeasonCompPeriod writes the comp at organization and league creation (idempotent; same row); one slugifyOrgName (lib/utils) for both start forms and both create routes; the leftover invited-panel and divider rules in auth.module.css removed; Home's gate reads plainly. Skipped on purpose: one copy of the door instead of two (Part 1's storage is on production); a per-plan promo callback on PricingSection; a shared "would the step open" helper across Home, the two pages and the two create routes; a server-component split of /auth/signup; merging the account-only form into the start form.

/review (2026-10-19, high risk, five lenses; gate green for this scope, check:layout admin-onboarding ✓ at four widths; the start and sign-up forms are not in the layout registry):

  • Fixed (Medium): the plan-step rule keyed on the browser-written plan mark — now server facts (above); mutation-checked (the plan mark or the tournament check put back each fail the guard).
  • Fixed (Low): the plan card's $0 could go stale after a choice on the same page — it is asked again whenever the chooser appears and shown only for the state it was asked in; a newer pricing-page plan in the address beats the one remembered at sign-up; a second submit that races past the account check gets the same 409; the lock-or-undo also catches a thrown error; the team and league pages keep Part 1's localhost behaviour; Club is ruled out before the window in the plan-step rule; the data dictionary no longer names the sign-up as a comp writer.
  • Accepted: two tabs on step 2 at once can each make an organization (the single-organization check is not atomic — as before); a failed comp write at creation still clears the lock (logged, as before); an undo that itself fails leaves an unconfirmed account behind (two admin failures in a row); for an account that chose the dark look, step 1 shows the warm card on the dark sign-in ground; the add-organization route has no rate limit (as before); the startup-tasks route lets any member mark a task (pre-existing — it can only close the first run, never reopen it).

Accepted, left as they are:

  • League door accounts made between Part 1's release and this one carry no locked copy; League self-sign-up is off everywhere but localhost, so nobody is affected.
  • The plan step's "Welcome to your Founding Season" banner still reads the window, so an organization that gets Tournament Plus free on its first choice after the close does not see it (a neighbour, not built here).

Coach Premium and the claim link, account first. app/team/TeamSignupClient.tsx is two steps on the same card (the sales page beside it unchanged): signed out, step 1 is the account alone — Create / Sign in kept, the step line ("1 Your account · 2 Your team", D3), Create account with no arrow (D7), the drawn fine print; signed in, step 2 is today's signed-in card (team, sport, plan, Start free / checkout) after "Your email is confirmed." when the link brought them (D5).   • /api/auth/team-signup: the coach sign-up's throttle (7bbfbebb); **an existing-account check before the sign-up link** (it had none — a sign-up link for an existing address can overwrite that account's password; the other sign-ups always checked); the door remembered, and locked for the offer (lockStartDoorOrUndo). The link returns to the claim (/coaches/claim/<token>?confirmed=1), the reactivation, or /coaches/start?confirmed=1.

A claim sign-up remembers no door either (/review): Home's Continue setup and a resend from sign-in would have opened the blank Premium step, where a new team could be bought and the claim left open. Its own email link returns to the claim; the organizer's claim email is the way back. Its door is still locked, so the offer after the close holds for the claim (edge (b)). A reactivation sign-up claims no door at all (a returning coach, not a start).
  • Founding Season, edge (b): create-team-checkout reads foundingSeasonOfferFor(user, 'premium'); /coaches/start and the claim page pass the card the same answer (foundingOffer), so the price shown is the price charged.
  • Home: the waiting Premium card hides while the Premium checkout is closed (the page shows an interest form) and once the account owns a live Premium portal.
  • Guards: account-first-signup (Part 3 block; mutation-checked 2026-10-19 — the draft put back, the existing-account check disabled or moved after the link, and the checkout back on the bare window each fail it); coach-signup-throttle-guard holds Coach Premium's limits.

/simplify (2026-10-19, four lenses): who is signed in comes from the server (no session check in the browser, no flash of the wrong step); one step line, components/auth/StartSteps, shared by the start forms and the Premium card; foundingSeasonOfferFor takes a signed-out visitor (the window alone), so both Premium pages ask it directly; one billing reader (parseStartBilling); the shared normalizeBillingCycle; the gated and error notices defined once, above each step's button; one submit label; Home's two Premium reads run together. Skipped on purpose: one sign-up guard shared by the three sign-up routes (a shared limiter pools budgets on security routes — a deliberate call for later); a shared "would the step open" helper across Home, the pages and the create routes.

/review (2026-10-19, high risk, five lenses; typecheck, lint, tokens, contrast, spelling green for this scope; check:layout n/a — the Premium page is not in the layout registry): no way found to get the Premium comp without the entitlement. Fixed: signing in on the card refreshes the page's answers (the offer was a signed-out visitor's, so after the close a held offer showed the list price); a waiting account that signs in on the card gets the check-your-email block with its resend (it was a dead end); a claim remembers no door and a reactivation claims none (above); a reactivated portal clears the door and its lock (lib/team-checkout.ts, as first provisioning does); the reactivation link keeps its team name, and a reactivation opens on Sign in; back from the link without a session opens on Sign in; one submit at a time; Home's Premium card hides when its reads fail; the Premium UAT smoke spec follows the two steps. Accepted: the shared sign-up limit can be spent by a spammer (as the coach sign-up's); "an account already exists" tells that one does (as every sign-up); the existing-account check scans the account list (as every sign-up); an account that began the old one-form Premium sign-up before this release and checks out after December 31 has no lock (it checked out at the link in the old flow); after an in-card sign-in the remembered billing is not re-applied.

Owed before this project closes: review the plan chooser (owner, 2026-10-19, walking §343 W5)

The plan step a new organization lands on after naming itself (/admin/onboarding?choosePlan=1) gets its own review toward the end of this project, before the plan is archived. The owner's notes from W5:

  • Old type and colours. It is still on the pre-warm look (the monospace pricing cards), not the portal's.
  • Too much feature list. Four cards of plan descriptions, twice-stated heading ("Start free or choose an upgrade" as the page title AND the card title), for a person who already chose a plan on the pricing page.
  • The buttons are far below the fold. The choose buttons sit under the descriptions and prices, out of sight on a laptop screen.
  • Nothing is highlighted when the plan picked is not on sale. W5 arrived with plan=league&billing=annual: Annual was chosen, but no card was featured. That is the code's rule, not a regression: PricingSection never features a gated card (isFeatured = !isGated && …), and League Plus is "Not open yet", so the chooser shows no highlight at all (Tournament Plus loses its default one too). The walk's expectation was written without checking that. The real question for the review: what should someone who came for League Plus see when League Plus is not open? Today nothing at the top says so; their plan is the third card, labelled Not open yet. Decide that in the review (likely candidates: say it plainly above the cards and offer the interest form, or keep them off this step entirely until League opens) rather than patching the highlight alone.

Draw it as a whole-screen before/after on the hub and run /design on it before asking the owner.
